rich_summary: Vahuka (the disguised Nala) witnesses King Rituparna’s astonishing ability to instantly calculate the number of leaves and fruits on a Vibhitaka tree. In exchange for revealing this numerical and dice knowledge, Nala offers his unmatched mastery of horses. When Nala learns the science of dice, the malevolent spirit Kali—who had possessed him since his gambling downfall—can no longer remain within him and is forced out, weakened by Damayanti’s curse and the serpent Karkotaka’s poison. Kali begs forgiveness, promising that those who recite Nala’s story will be safe from him. Freed from this influence, Nala drives Rituparna swiftly to Vidarbha. Meanwhile, Damayanti hears the unmistakable thunder of Nala’s chariot and hopes desperately that her lost husband has finally returned.

highlight_spans.why: Introduces the remarkable calculation challenge with the Vibhitaka tree, setting up the exchange of knowledge between Rituparna and Vahuka.
The moment when Rituparna shares the science of dice and Nala offers his horse‑lore, a pivotal knowledge exchange that changes Nala’s fate.
Kali emerging from Nala’s body marks the spiritual turning point where Nala is freed from the force that caused his downfall.
Damayanti’s emotional monologue reveals her unwavering love and despair, heightening the anticipation of Nala’s return.

top_scenes.scene_text: Vahuka cuts down the Vibhitaka tree and counts its fruits while the astonished king Rituparna watches beside the chariot in the forest.
A dark spectral Kali erupts from Nala’s body in a cloud of poison while the freed king stands resolute beside the fallen Vibhitaka tree.
Damayanti stands on a palace terrace at sunset, listening to the thunderous chariot approaching as peacocks and elephants cry out across the city.
